Enterprise environmental factors are conditions outside the team's control, and backlog items describe work to build rather than reusable internal assets.  Takeaway: Internal templates and historical repositories the team can reuse are organizational process assets.
choices: Organizational process assets, because they are internal resources the project can use
Enterprise environmental factors, because they originate outside the organization
Product backlog items, because each one describes a feature the team must build
Constraints, because the team is never allowed to tailor or adjust them

questions.question: A manager asks the Scrum Master to assign each task to a specific developer and to report daily on who is falling behind. Why does this conflict with the Scrum Master role?
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is a servant leader who coaches, facilitates, and helps remove impediments rather than assigning tasks and policing members. Ordering the backlog belongs to the Product Owner, and selecting the sprint workload belongs to the Developers.  Takeaway: The Scrum Master serves and facilitates the team; it is not a command-and-control role.
choices: The Scrum Master serves the team by coaching and facilitating, not by commanding and controlling members
The Scrum Master is the only person allowed to order the product backlog by value
The Scrum Master must personally write, review, and complete all of the developers' code during each sprint
The Scrum Master alone decides how many items go into every sprint for the team

questions.question: Which statement best describes the project-management process groups?
questions.explanation: Process groups are logical groupings of project-management activities, not project phases. They overlap and recur across the life of a project or a single phase, so planning, executing, and monitoring and controlling happen repeatedly and concurrently. Treating them as one-time sequential phases, or claiming executing must fully end before monitoring can begin, misrepresents how the activities actually interact.  Takeaway: Process groups are overlapping, recurring activity categories, not sequential project phases.
choices: They are categories of activities that overlap and can recur throughout a project or phase
They are the sequential life-cycle phases a project passes through exactly once, in a fixed predetermined order
Monitoring and Controlling starts only after Executing has fully finished
Each process group runs exactly once and never repeats during the project

questions.question: An analyst completes the business case for a proposed drone-delivery pilot and finds the costs clearly outweigh any realistic benefit. Feeling pressure because executives are excited about the idea, she wonders what the business case is even for. What is the correct understanding?
questions.explanation: The purpose of a business case is to determine whether an investment is justified, and a valid outcome is a recommendation not to proceed when the analysis shows costs exceed benefits, so an honest negative recommendation is exactly its job. Assuming it must always endorse the project, or manipulating the figures, defeats the reason the analysis is done.  Takeaway: A business case may recommend not proceeding; its job is honest justification, not automatic approval.
choices: A business case exists to approve projects, so once it is written the project should always move forward.
A negative business case should be quietly revised until the numbers finally support launching the pilot.
A business case can legitimately recommend not proceeding when the costs outweigh the expected benefits.
The business case cannot recommend against a project; only the sponsor may cancel it after the charter is signed.

questions.question: An instructor asks a CAPM candidate to define a project life cycle. Which description is most accurate?
questions.explanation: A project life cycle is the series of phases a project moves through from initiation to completion. The charter-signing ceremony, the stakeholder roster, and the post-handover operations period are separate concepts and do not describe the life cycle.  Takeaway: A project life cycle is the set of phases from start to completion.
choices: The single ceremony in which the sponsor formally signs the project charter.
The complete roster of every stakeholder who holds an interest in the project.
The ongoing operational period that begins after the product is handed over.
The series of phases a project passes through from its start to its completion.

questions.question: A new team member asks what a work breakdown structure is actually for on a predictive project. Which TWO statements correctly describe the purpose of a WBS?
questions.explanation: A WBS decomposes the total project scope into manageable deliverables and work packages and provides the framework for estimating, scheduling, and control. Sequencing and dependencies belong to the network diagram, activity dates belong to the schedule, and risks belong to the risk register; none of these are what a WBS shows.  Takeaway: The WBS organizes deliverable-based scope and underpins estimating and control; it does not sequence or schedule activities.
choices: It breaks the total project scope into smaller, manageable deliverables
It provides the framework for estimating cost and duration and for control
It shows the sequence and dependencies among the project's activities
It records each activity's planned start and finish dates
It captures each identified risk together with its assigned response owner and planned trigger

questions.question: A project manager's weekly status meetings routinely run long and drift off topic, leaving decisions unmade. Which change would most improve the meetings' effectiveness?
questions.explanation: Effective meetings have a clear purpose, a focused agenda circulated ahead of time, the right attendees, and ground rules that keep the group on topic and moving to decisions. Adding everyone, removing time limits, or eliminating meetings entirely does not fix drift and can reduce coordination.  Takeaway: A focused agenda, the right attendees, and ground rules make status meetings effective.
choices: Distribute a focused agenda in advance and set ground rules that keep discussion on the listed topics
Invite every stakeholder in the organization so nobody feels left out of any discussion
Remove all time limits so every topic can be discussed until it is fully exhausted
Cancel the meetings and rely only on written status reports for all coordination

questions.question: The single environmental test chamber your project requires is contractually reserved to another division until March 31, a date already fixed and documented. For planning, this situation is best treated as:
questions.explanation: A constraint is a known limitation on the project, and a chamber reserved until a fixed, documented date restricts scheduling in a known way. A risk involves uncertainty about whether an event will occur, which does not fit a date that is already settled.  Takeaway: Known, fixed limitations are constraints; uncertain future events are risks.
choices: A risk, because the chamber's availability is genuinely uncertain
An issue, since the reserved chamber has already caused a delay
An assumption, because you expect the chamber to be free eventually
A constraint, because the known unavailability limits your options

questions.question: A team wants to know what single commitment gives the developers focus and coherence throughout a sprint. What is it?
questions.explanation: The sprint goal is the commitment associated with the sprint backlog, giving the developers a single objective and coherence during the sprint. The definition of done is the commitment tied to the increment, and the product goal is tied to the product backlog.  Takeaway: The sprint goal is the sprint's single unifying commitment.
choices: The definition of done
The sprint goal
The product goal
The velocity target

questions.question: Arrange the requirements activities in the order a business analyst typically begins them (they overlap and iterate in practice).
questions.explanation: A business analyst typically begins by planning the analysis approach, then eliciting needs, analyzing and modeling them, validating that they deliver the right value, and managing and tracing the approved requirements. In practice these overlap and iterate, and requirements management and traceability are maintained continuously - not only after validation. The order shown is the usual starting sequence, not a strict one-way gate.  Takeaway: Plan, elicit, analyze, validate, then manage - but the activities overlap and iterate, with traceability maintained throughout.
sequence: Plan the business analysis approach
Elicit the requirements from stakeholders
Analyze and model the requirements
Validate the requirements with stakeholders
Manage and trace the approved requirements

questions.question: Which term describes the work defined at the lowest level of the work breakdown structure, where cost and duration can be estimated and progress managed?
questions.explanation: A work package is the work at the lowest level of the WBS, small enough that its cost and duration can be reliably estimated and its progress managed. A control account is a higher-level management control point that groups work packages, a milestone is a zero-duration event, and a phase is a broad grouping of activities ending in deliverables, so none of those is the lowest-level work element.  Takeaway: A work package is the lowest-level WBS component where cost and duration are estimated.
choices: Control account
Work package
Milestone
Project phase

questions.question: In which organizational structure is authority shared roughly equally between the project manager and the functional manager?
questions.explanation: A balanced matrix splits authority roughly equally between the project manager and the functional manager. The strong and weak matrix labels are reversed here: a strong matrix gives the project manager the greater share of authority, while a weak matrix leaves most authority with the functional manager. A projectized structure concentrates authority in the project manager rather than dividing it.  Takeaway: Weak matrix favors the functional manager, strong matrix favors the project manager, and balanced matrix shares authority roughly equally.
choices: Strong matrix, where the functional manager holds nearly all of the authority
Weak matrix, where the project manager holds nearly all of the authority
Projectized, where authority is divided evenly between two competing managers
Balanced matrix, where authority is shared between the project and functional managers

questions.question: A risk is judged very likely to occur and, if it does, would seriously delay delivery. How is its overall risk rating typically derived?
questions.explanation: A risk's rating is produced by combining how likely the event is with how large its effect would be. Budget size, how many people raise it, and the reporter's seniority do not determine the rating.  Takeaway: Risk rating combines probability of occurrence with severity of impact.
choices: From the total size of the approved project budget
From how many stakeholders happen to mention it
By combining the probability of the event with the magnitude of its impact
From the seniority of whoever first raised the risk

questions.question: A stakeholder asks how solution scope differs from product scope on a new payroll project. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Solution scope is broad: the full set of changes needed to deliver value, such as process redesign, training, and the product itself, whereas product scope is narrower, covering the features and functions of the product. Option B reverses the two, and the others equate scope with code or with schedule and budget.  Takeaway: Product scope is the product's features; solution scope is everything (process, people, and product) needed to deliver the value.
choices: Solution scope is the project schedule, while product scope is the project budget.
Product scope covers all the work, process changes, and training needed to deploy the solution, while solution scope lists only the product's own features and functions.
Solution scope and product scope both refer only to the software's code and nothing else.
Solution scope covers everything needed to deliver the solution, process changes and training included, while product scope is the product's own features and functions.

questions.question: During refinement, the team cannot size a story because too many technical unknowns remain, so no reliable estimate is possible. Which INVEST characteristic is most clearly missing?
questions.explanation: INVEST calls for a story to be estimable, meaning the team can produce a reasonable size for it; unresolved unknowns that block any estimate mean that characteristic is missing. Valuable concerns user benefit and independent concerns ordering dependencies, neither of which is the problem described.  Takeaway: If unknowns block any reliable sizing, the story fails the 'Estimable' of INVEST.
choices: Negotiable, because the story's details were locked in far too early
Valuable, because the story provides no benefit to any user or customer
Independent, because the story cannot be built until another one is finished
Estimable, because the team cannot produce a reliable size for the story

questions.question: A newly identified risk about database performance is being assigned an owner. Which statement about the risk owner is correct?
questions.explanation: A risk owner is the individual assigned to watch a specific risk and carry out its response, chosen for being well positioned to do so, and this is often a team member rather than the project manager. Making the project manager or sponsor the default owner, or rotating ownership arbitrarily, ignores who can actually manage the risk.  Takeaway: The risk owner is whoever can best monitor and respond to that risk, not automatically the PM.
choices: The owner is whoever is best positioned to monitor the risk and act on its response
The sponsor automatically owns any risk that is rated high
Ownership rotates through the whole team on a weekly basis
The project manager must personally own every risk on the project

questions.question: A new associate is asked which three documents together make up the scope baseline. Which set is correct?
questions.explanation: The scope baseline is the approved scope statement, the WBS, and the WBS dictionary. Sets that pull in the charter, requirements list, risk register, schedule baseline, or cost baseline mix in documents that belong to other baselines or plans.  Takeaway: The scope baseline is the scope statement plus the WBS plus the WBS dictionary.
choices: The scope statement, the schedule baseline, and the cost baseline.
The requirements list, the risk register, and the WBS.
The project charter, the schedule baseline, and the cost baseline.
The project scope statement, the WBS, and the WBS dictionary.

questions.question: In Scrum, which statement best describes the increment?
questions.explanation: The increment is the usable output of a sprint, made up of completed work that meets the definition of done and builds on prior increments. The ordered list of needs is the product backlog, and the single sprint objective is the sprint goal.  Takeaway: The increment is usable, done work meeting the definition of done.
choices: The ordered list of everything the product might ever need
The 15-minute event where developers plan the coming day
The single objective the developers commit to for the sprint
The sum of usable, done work that meets the definition of done

questions.question: A team using an adaptive approach asks whether milestones have any place in their work, since they plan in short iterations. What is the best response?
questions.explanation: Milestones are zero-duration markers of significant points and apply regardless of approach, so an adaptive team can still use them for a release or a major review. Confining milestones to predictive schedules or requiring a predictive conversion misstates that a milestone is simply a point of significance.  Takeaway: Milestones mark significant points and are used in both predictive and adaptive approaches.
choices: No, milestones apply only to predictive schedules that use fixed calendar dates
No, once a backlog exists the iterations replace milestones entirely
Yes, milestones mark significant points and stay useful in adaptive work
Yes, but only if each iteration is first converted into a predictive plan

questions.question: An indie studio is building a first-of-its-kind virtual-reality experience; player preferences are unknown and will only be learned through repeated playtesting, and stakeholders want a playable build to try roughly every month. Which approach fits best, and why?
questions.explanation: An adaptive approach is chosen when requirements are uncertain and likely to change and stakeholders want frequent, incremental value, both of which describe this VR experience. Predictive and waterfall approaches lock scope early and are ill-suited to requirements that will only be discovered through playtesting.  Takeaway: Uncertain, evolving requirements plus a need for frequent value point to an adaptive approach.
choices: Predictive, because a full plan written up front will keep the requirements from shifting later.
Waterfall, because running strict sequential phases will get the experience to market sooner.
Predictive, because delivering early playable builds would first require a completely frozen scope baseline.
Adaptive, because it welcomes changing requirements and delivers usable value in short cycles.

questions.question: A project team is unsure who champions their initiative to senior management and secures the money it needs to move forward. Which role fills that responsibility?
questions.explanation: The sponsor champions the project within the organization and provides the funding needed to proceed, and also authorizes the charter. Building deliverables and integrating the daily work are team and project-manager responsibilities, and an auditor has no funding role.  Takeaway: The sponsor champions and funds the project and authorizes the charter.
choices: The team members, who build the technical deliverables
An external auditor brought in to review the project
The project manager, who integrates the daily work
The project sponsor, who champions and funds the project

questions.question: A company must build a bridge inspection system to a fixed engineering specification mandated by a safety regulator, with no expected changes and well-understood steps. Which approach is the better fit and why?
questions.explanation: A predictive approach fits when requirements are stable and the work follows a well-understood, low-change process, which describes a fixed regulator-mandated specification. Adaptive approaches are chosen for high uncertainty and expected change, so they are not the better fit here.  Takeaway: Stable, well-understood, low-change work favors a predictive approach.
choices: Adaptive, because fixed specifications always benefit from frequent scope changes
Predictive, because the requirements are stable and the process is well understood
Adaptive, because any regulated project must deliver in short experimental cycles
Predictive, because predictive approaches forbid ever gathering stakeholder feedback

questions.question: Match each cost estimate class to its typical accuracy range.
questions.explanation: A ROM estimate is made earliest with the widest range; a budget estimate narrows it as scope firms up; a definitive estimate is the tightest, made late with full detail. These bands are common, illustrative ranges - actual ranges vary by organization, industry, and the estimate-class system in use. Because of progressive elaboration, accuracy improves over time; confusing ROM's wide band with the definitive band is the usual error.  Takeaway: Estimate ranges tighten from ROM to budget to definitive as the project's detail grows.
pairs: Rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimate
Formed very early with minimal detail; typical range -25% to +75%
Budget estimate
Formed during planning as scope firms up; typical range -10% to +25%
Definitive estimate
Formed late with full detail; typical range -5% to +10%
Effect of progressive elaboration
The estimate range narrows as the project advances and more detail becomes known

questions.question: Who is generally in the best position to provide effort estimates for the activities that create the deliverables?
questions.explanation: The people who will do the work are best placed to estimate the effort it takes. The sponsor funds the project, the customer defines needs, and an outside auditor lacks the hands-on knowledge to estimate the work accurately.  Takeaway: The team members who do the work are best positioned to estimate it.
choices: The sponsor, because they control the funding
The team members who will perform the work
The customer, because they defined the requirements
An external auditor with no role on the project

questions.question: On a Kanban team's cumulative flow diagram, the vertical band for the 'In Progress' state grows steadily wider over several weeks while the 'Done' band rises only slowly. What does this pattern most likely indicate?
questions.explanation: On a cumulative flow diagram the vertical width of a state's band is the amount of work in that state. A widening 'In Progress' band with a slowly rising 'Done' band means items enter faster than they leave, a bottleneck that increases work in progress and cycle time. It is not rising throughput, reduced scope, or tighter WIP limits, which would narrow the band.  Takeaway: On a cumulative flow diagram, a widening in-progress band signals growing WIP and a bottleneck, not faster delivery.
choices: The team's throughput is steadily rising, so completed items are being finished faster with each passing week
Work in progress is piling up faster than it is finished, signaling a bottleneck that lengthens cycle time
The project's total scope has been reduced over the period
The team has tightened its work-in-progress limits to speed up flow

questions.question: A team scores each candidate feature on expected benefit and on the work required, then chooses high-benefit, low-effort items first. Which prioritization approach is this?
questions.explanation: Weighing each item's value against its effort to pick high value for low effort is value-versus-effort prioritization. Kano classifies by satisfaction type and MoSCoW groups by obligation, neither of which is a direct value-to-effort tradeoff.  Takeaway: Value-versus-effort prioritization favors high-value, low-effort items first.
choices: Kano analysis, which sorts features into basic, performance, and delighter categories
MoSCoW, which groups items into Must, Should, Could, and Won't categories
First-in-first-out, which takes whichever request happened to arrive earliest
Value-versus-effort, which favors high-value items that need relatively little work

questions.question: Halfway through a two-week iteration, an agile team discovers valuable new work. According to iteration-based practice, how should they usually handle it?
questions.explanation: In iteration-based agile the timebox length stays fixed, so new work is placed on the backlog and pulled into a future iteration rather than disrupting the current one. Extending the timebox, canceling the iteration, or swapping the goal mid-iteration all break the protection a fixed timebox provides.  Takeaway: Timeboxes stay fixed; new work waits in the backlog for a later iteration.
choices: Immediately extend the current iteration's length to absorb the new work
Cancel the current iteration and restart planning from the beginning
Replace the current sprint goal with the new work in mid-iteration
Add the new work to the backlog and consider it for a future iteration

questions.question: A startup plans to launch a bare version of its app to learn whether commuters will pay for real-time parking data before building more. A stakeholder worries this means shipping a broken product. Which statement best describes an MVP?
questions.explanation: An MVP is the smallest usable version that lets the team test key assumptions and gain validated learning, which is different from a broken product. It is not all the Must-haves bundled together, not a hidden throwaway prototype, and it is deliberately small rather than maximal in scope.  Takeaway: An MVP is the smallest usable release that yields validated learning - not broken, not all the Must-haves.
choices: It is the release that bundles together every Must-have item the team identified
It is the smallest usable version that produces validated learning, not a broken or low-quality release
It is a throwaway prototype that real users are never allowed to see or use
It is the version built with the largest possible scope to impress early investors

questions.question: An activity needs 24 hours of effort. Two team members are assigned and each works on it 4 hours per day. Expressed as work periods, what is the activity's duration?
questions.explanation: Duration counts work periods, and 24 hours of effort at 8 combined hours per day spans three work days. Total effort of 24 hours measures the labor consumed rather than elapsed periods, and duration is stated in work periods rather than calendar time that folds in nonworking days.  Takeaway: Duration is the count of work periods, derived from effort and daily availability.
choices: 24 hours, since the duration equals the total effort recorded for the activity
3 work days, the number of work periods needed to complete the effort
6 work days, because each person separately needs 24 hours of their own time
3 calendar days, counting the weekends and holidays inside the span

questions.question: A coach tells a new Scrum team that they are violating Scrum because they do not track velocity. Is this correct?
questions.explanation: Velocity is an optional forecasting aid rather than a required element of Scrum, so a team can practice Scrum without formally tracking it. It is also distinct from capacity and is not a prerequisite for setting a sprint goal.  Takeaway: Velocity is optional in Scrum, not a mandated artifact.
choices: Yes, velocity is a mandatory Scrum artifact that every team must report each sprint
No, velocity is a helpful but optional forecasting aid, not a required Scrum artifact
Yes, without a velocity number the team cannot set any sprint goal at all
No, because velocity is identical to capacity and is therefore tracked automatically

questions.question: A development team wants to adopt continuous integration, test-driven development, and pair programming to raise code quality. These disciplined engineering practices are most associated with which approach?
questions.explanation: Extreme Programming is centered on disciplined engineering practices such as continuous integration, test-driven development, and pair programming. Kanban focuses on flow, Scrum on events and accountabilities, and SAFe on scaling, so none of those is defined by these coding practices.  Takeaway: XP is the engineering-practice approach.
choices: Kanban
Scrum
SAFe
Extreme Programming

questions.question: A finished patient-scheduling system is being turned over to the IT operations group that will run and maintain it going forward. This handover is best described as:
questions.explanation: Handing a completed product to the group that will operate and maintain it is a transition performed as part of closing. It is not a fresh planning phase, an issue, or a risk response.  Takeaway: Closing includes transitioning the product to operations or the customer.
choices: The start of a brand-new planning phase for the same project
A transition of the product to operations as part of closing
An issue that must be escalated to the project sponsor
A risk response drawn straight from the risk register

questions.question: A project's critical path is fully staffed, but two activities on it need the same specialist during the same week, exceeding that person's availability. The team must resolve the over-allocation even if the finish date moves. Which technique are they applying?
questions.explanation: Resource leveling adjusts the schedule to keep resource usage within available limits; because it can delay activities on the critical path, it may change the critical path and push out the finish date. Resource smoothing, by contrast, only uses free and total float and does not change the finish date. Fast tracking and crashing are schedule-compression techniques for shortening duration, not for resolving an over-allocated resource.  Takeaway: Resource leveling respects resource limits and can move the finish date; resource smoothing stays within float and does not.
choices: Resource smoothing, because the finish date is never allowed to change
Resource leveling, which adjusts the schedule to respect resource limits and may change the critical path and finish date
Fast tracking, because activities are being run in parallel to save time
Crashing, because extra budget is added to shorten the schedule

questions.question: A project manager charts, for each key stakeholder, how engaged they are today against how engaged the project needs them to be. What is this comparison used to do?
questions.explanation: Comparing current versus desired engagement highlights gaps that the team then plans actions to close. It is not a budgeting tool, it does not set milestones, and it is unrelated to accepting deliverables.  Takeaway: Assessing current versus desired engagement exposes gaps to be closed with planned actions.
choices: Calculate the project's total labor budget
Establish the zero-duration milestones on the schedule
Reveal gaps so the team can plan actions to close them
Grant formal acceptance of the final deliverables

questions.question: A manager asserts, "Our portfolio must contain only tightly related projects, because that relatedness is what lets a portfolio deliver one combined benefit." What is the most accurate correction?
questions.explanation: Portfolio components are chosen to advance strategy and need not relate to one another, whereas obtaining a combined benefit from related components is what defines a program. Claiming a portfolio holds only related components, equating a portfolio with a program, or restricting it to operations all misstate the definitions.  Takeaway: Portfolio components need not relate; combined benefit from related components describes a program.
choices: The manager is correct; a portfolio holds only components that are closely and directly related to one another, and that shared relatedness is exactly what lets it deliver one combined benefit.
A portfolio and a program are simply two names for the same thing, so its components are always related.
Portfolio components are selected to advance strategy and need not relate; delivering a combined benefit from related components describes a program.
A portfolio may hold only ongoing operations, so its components are by nature never related in any way.

questions.question: Early in discovery, a team wants to generate the widest possible range of ideas for a new loyalty program before evaluating any of them. Which technique fits this goal best?
questions.explanation: Brainstorming is designed to generate a large volume of ideas quickly while deferring judgment, which fits early, open-ended idea generation. Document review studies existing materials, observing one cashier captures current behavior rather than new ideas, and verifying software against a spec checks conformance instead of creating options.  Takeaway: Use brainstorming to generate many ideas early, deferring judgment until later.
choices: A formal document review of the current loyalty program's existing contract terms.
A brainstorming session that gathers many ideas freely without judging them yet.
Observation of a single cashier enrolling customers in the program at the register.
A verification test that checks the existing loyalty software against its specification.

questions.question: Developers occasionally need to consult a large coding-standards handbook that rarely changes, but only when a specific question arises. Which communication method best fits?
questions.explanation: Pull communication such as a wiki or repository lets developers retrieve large reference material whenever they actually need it. Emailing the whole handbook daily floods inboxes with content most will not use, a recurring read-through wastes time on rarely needed detail, and a verbal briefing leaves nothing to look up later.  Takeaway: Use pull communication for large reference content people access on demand.
choices: Push communication that emails the full handbook to every developer at the start of each day.
Interactive communication scheduled as a recurring meeting to read through the handbook aloud.
A single verbal briefing on the handbook, with no written copy kept for anyone afterward.
Pull communication, such as a wiki or repository the developers consult on demand.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a project phase in a predictive life cycle?
questions.explanation: A project phase is a collection of logically related activities that ends with the completion of one or more deliverables, often at a phase gate. A category of management activities such as planning describes a process group, a zero-duration significant event describes a milestone, and the lowest-level component of the WBS is a work package, so those describe different concepts.  Takeaway: A phase is a group of related activities ending in deliverables; do not confuse it with a process group or a milestone.
choices: A collection of logically related project activities that culminates in the completion of one or more deliverables
A category of project-management activities such as planning or executing
A zero-duration point that marks a significant event or approval
The lowest-level component of the work breakdown structure

questions.question: Match each incentive contract type to its description.
questions.explanation: FPIF caps the price and flexes the fee with performance; CPIF reimburses costs and adjusts the fee by formula; CPAF reimburses costs and pays an award set by the buyer's judgment. CPFF, by contrast, pays a fixed fee that never moves. Mixing CPIF's formula-based fee with CPAF's subjective award is the common trap.  Takeaway: Incentive fees flex with performance (FPIF, CPIF), an award fee reflects the buyer's judgment (CPAF), and a fixed fee never changes (CPFF).
pairs: Fixed price incentive fee (FPIF)
A price with a ceiling; the fee rises or falls with performance against a target cost
Cost plus incentive fee (CPIF)
Costs are reimbursed plus a fee that varies by formula for meeting cost or performance targets
Cost plus award fee (CPAF)
Costs are reimbursed plus an award the buyer grants based on a subjective performance judgment
Cost plus fixed fee (CPFF)
Costs are reimbursed plus a set fee that does not change regardless of performance

questions.question: On a streaming service, subscribers grow steadily more satisfied as video start-up time gets shorter and steadily less satisfied as it grows longer. In the Kano model, start-up speed here is which kind of feature?
questions.explanation: A performance feature moves satisfaction up or down in proportion to how much is provided, which fits start-up speed that steadily changes satisfaction. A must-be feature is an expected basic whose presence is barely noticed, and a delighter is an unexpected surprise rather than a linear factor.  Takeaway: A Kano performance feature scales satisfaction with the amount delivered.
choices: A performance feature, because satisfaction rises and falls in proportion to how much is delivered
A must-be feature, because its absence dissatisfies while its presence goes unnoticed
A delighter, because fast start-up is an unexpected surprise users never anticipate
An indifferent feature, because subscribers do not notice start-up time at all

questions.question: A shipyard builds a ferry's steel hull on a fixed, plan-based schedule while developing the ferry's passenger booking software in short, feedback-driven sprints. Which development approach is in use?
questions.explanation: A hybrid approach deliberately combines predictive and adaptive methods on the same project, which fits scheduling the hull predictively while building the software in sprints. Labeling it purely predictive or purely adaptive ignores that both styles are in use at the same time.  Takeaway: Combining predictive and adaptive work on one project is a hybrid approach.
choices: Hybrid, because it combines predictive and adaptive methods within one project.
Purely predictive, because the overall project follows a defined schedule.
Purely adaptive, because the team is running software sprints.
Iterative only, because the booking software is refined over repeated cycles.

questions.question: Order these organizational structures from LEAST to MOST project-manager authority.
questions.explanation: PM authority rises along the spectrum functional (least) -> weak matrix -> balanced matrix -> strong matrix -> projectized (most). Option B reverses it, C scrambles the order, and D is false because authority clearly differs by structure.  Takeaway: PM authority: functional < weak < balanced < strong matrix < projectized.
choices: Functional, weak matrix, balanced matrix, strong matrix, projectized.
Projectized, strong matrix, balanced matrix, weak matrix, functional.
Functional, projectized, weak matrix, strong matrix, balanced matrix.
They all give the project manager roughly equal authority.

questions.question: During a tense review a stakeholder is upset about a decision. The project manager listens closely and genuinely understands the stakeholder's feelings and viewpoint, yet still believes the decision is correct. This behavior best reflects:
questions.explanation: Empathy is understanding another person's perspective and feelings, which does not require agreeing with them or changing the decision. Holding the decision is not a self-management failure, the manager did listen genuinely, and empathy does not demand agreement.  Takeaway: Empathy means understanding another's perspective, not necessarily agreeing with it.
choices: Poor self-management, because the manager did not change the decision
Manipulation, because the manager was only pretending to listen
A failure of empathy, since empathy requires agreeing with the stakeholder
Empathy, which means understanding another's perspective without necessarily agreeing

questions.question: Before engaging stakeholders on replacing an inventory system, an analyst wants to understand the current business rules and the pitfalls encountered on a similar past rollout. Which combination fits best?
questions.explanation: Document analysis of existing materials plus a lessons-learned review surfaces current business rules and known past pitfalls, which is the right groundwork before engaging people. Brainstorming with no preparation is premature, relying on manager memory is unreliable, and dismissing written records ignores a valuable source of existing rules.  Takeaway: Start with document analysis and lessons learned to understand existing rules and past pitfalls.
choices: A large brainstorming session held before any groundwork or preparation is done.
A survey asking managers to recall every current business rule purely from memory.
Document analysis of existing materials together with a review of lessons learned.
Observation only, on the belief that written records are never worth reading at all.

questions.question: Midway through a bakery's equipment upgrade, the newly installed oven fails inspection and cannot be used, halting production right now. Is this an issue or a risk?
questions.explanation: An issue is a condition or event that has already happened and requires action now, which fits the oven that has already failed and stopped production. A risk is a future, uncertain event, so it does not describe something that has already occurred.  Takeaway: Already happened is an issue; future and uncertain is a risk.
choices: A risk, because the failed oven may eventually delay the project's overall schedule.
An issue, because it is a condition that has already occurred and needs resolving now.
An assumption, because the team had taken for granted that the oven would pass inspection.
A constraint, because the failed inspection now limits what the project team can do.

questions.question: A team plans the immediate work in fine detail now and leaves later work at a high level, adding detail as more becomes known. What is this planning approach called?
questions.explanation: Progressive elaboration develops the plan in increasing detail as information becomes available, and rolling-wave planning is a common form of it. It is legitimate planning - not scope creep (uncontrolled scope growth), not gold-plating (unrequested extras), and not change control.  Takeaway: Adding detail as you learn = progressive elaboration, not scope change.
choices: Progressive elaboration (often via rolling-wave planning).
Scope creep, because detail is added over time.
Gold-plating, because the plan keeps growing.
Integrated change control of the scope baseline.

questions.question: Several related projects are coordinated together so the organization gains benefits it could not achieve by managing each project separately. What is this coordinated grouping called?
questions.explanation: A program is a group of related projects managed together to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually. A portfolio is a strategic collection whose components need not relate, a project is a single temporary effort, and operations are ongoing - none fits 'related projects coordinated for shared benefit.'  Takeaway: Program = related projects coordinated for benefits you can't get separately.
choices: A program - related projects coordinated together for shared benefits.
A portfolio - an often-unrelated collection chosen purely by strategy.
A single large project directed by one manager.
Ongoing operations that sustain the business.

questions.question: An analyst needs deep, detailed insight into the undocumented logic that one senior compliance officer applies when approving policy exceptions. Which elicitation technique fits best?
questions.explanation: An interview draws out depth and detail from one individual, which suits probing a single expert's undocumented reasoning. A survey gathers breadth across many respondents rather than depth, brainstorming generates new ideas instead of capturing an existing practice, and a marketing brochure does not reveal the officer's logic.  Takeaway: Use interviews for depth from an individual; use surveys for breadth across many.
choices: A broad survey sent to the entire compliance department for fast, quick input.
A one-on-one interview with the senior compliance officer.
A brainstorming session held to invent brand-new exception-handling ideas.
A review of the vendor's marketing brochure for the compliance software tool.

questions.question: A project manager reviews a new project's size, complexity, industry regulations, and team experience, then selects and adjusts which processes, tools, and life cycle the team will use rather than applying a fixed methodology unchanged. What is the project manager doing?
questions.explanation: Tailoring means deliberately selecting and adjusting the processes, tools, and life cycle to fit a project's unique context: its size, risk, regulation, and team. Progressive elaboration and rolling wave planning add detail to scope and schedule over time, and scope creep is uncontrolled scope growth; none describes fitting the approach to context.  Takeaway: Tailoring adapts the processes, methods, and life cycle to fit each project's specific context.
choices: Progressive elaboration
Rolling wave planning
Tailoring the approach
Scope creep

questions.question: A predictive team plans to release the business analyst as soon as the requirements are signed off, assuming no analysis work remains. Which statement is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Business analysis continues after sign-off because managing requirement changes and helping validate that the delivered solution meets the real need are ongoing activities. Sign-off is one milestone, not the end of the work, and taking over delivery is the project manager's responsibility rather than the analyst's.  Takeaway: Business analysis runs across the life cycle, continuing after sign-off through change management and validation.
choices: Correct, because once the requirements are baselined there is no further business analysis to perform on the project.
Correct, because business analysis applies only during initiation and never during the execution or closing of the work.
Incorrect, because business analysis continues afterward through managing changes and helping validate the delivered solution.
Incorrect, because the analyst must instead take over full delivery of the project once the requirements are signed.

questions.question: A stakeholder asks the project manager to start sending status updates through a personal messaging app, but the approved communications plan specifies a weekly email report. What should the project manager generally do?
questions.explanation: When a communications plan is already approved, the manager follows it and routes any desired change through the appropriate process rather than abandoning the plan on the spot. Switching immediately or halting reporting bypasses the plan, and dismissing the stakeholder ignores a legitimate request.  Takeaway: When a plan exists, follow it and handle changes through the proper process.
choices: Immediately switch all status reporting over to the messaging app
Halt all reporting until a completely new plan is written from scratch
Refuse the request, since stakeholders cannot influence reporting
Follow the approved communications plan and handle the change through the proper process

questions.question: A new analyst asks whether business analysis has a different purpose on predictive versus adaptive projects and whether the analyst sets the backlog order on adaptive work. Which statement is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Business analysis serves the same purpose in both approaches - understanding needs and defining requirements - but predictive baselines a specification under change control while adaptive continuously refines a backlog, and the analyst informs priority without owning the order. It is performed in both approaches, and the mechanisms differ, so they are not identical.  Takeaway: BA has one purpose across approaches; only the mechanism differs, and the BA never owns backlog order.
choices: The purpose is entirely different, and the analyst personally sets the backlog order on adaptive work
Business analysis is performed only on predictive projects, so adaptive work does not need it
The purpose is the same in both; predictive baselines a spec while adaptive refines a backlog, and the analyst does not own the order
The two are identical in every mechanism, including formal change control applied on both

questions.question: A product team builds a rough prototype of a single checkout screen, then reworks that same screen again and again from user feedback until it finally meets the need. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Iterative development refines and improves the same deliverable through successive cycles until it meets the need, which matches reworking the one checkout screen. Incremental delivery differs because it adds new usable pieces rather than reworking the same one, and a fixed up-front design describes predictive work.  Takeaway: Iterative means repeatedly refining the same deliverable.
choices: Incremental, because a new usable piece is added with each pass.
Predictive, because the screen's design was fixed completely in advance.
Iterative, because the same deliverable is refined through repeated cycles.
Hybrid, because two distinct approaches are deliberately combined here.

questions.question: A specialized crane crew has not yet confirmed whether it can be on site during your concrete pour window; the vendor says it depends on another job that may run long. For planning, this is best treated as:
questions.explanation: A risk is an uncertain event, and because the crew's availability is not yet known and hinges on another job, it is uncertain and belongs in the risk register. A constraint would apply only if the unavailability were a known, settled limitation.  Takeaway: Uncertain resource availability is a risk; a settled limitation is a constraint.
choices: A risk, because the crew's availability is uncertain and may or may not occur
A constraint, because the crew is already known to be unavailable
A milestone, because the concrete pour window is a significant point
A deliverable, because the crew produces a verifiable end result

questions.question: A CAPM candidate is asked what a project phase is. Which description is most accurate?
questions.explanation: A project phase is a collection of logically related activities that ends with the completion of one or more deliverables, and the phases in sequence make up the life cycle. A stakeholder list, the post-handover operations period, and the charter-signing meeting are separate concepts and do not define a phase.  Takeaway: A project phase is a group of related activities ending in one or more deliverables.
choices: The complete list of everyone who holds an interest in the outcome of the project.
A collection of logically related project activities that culminates in the completion of one or more deliverables.
The single ongoing period of routine operational work that begins only after the finished product has been handed over to the customer.
The one meeting in which the sponsor formally signs and authorizes the project charter.

questions.question: An enterprise has a dozen agile teams that must align their plans on a shared cadence over a multi-sprint horizon. Which framework is designed for this alignment, and what does its PI represent?
questions.explanation: SAFe is a scaling framework that aligns many teams on a shared cadence, and in SAFe the PI is the Planning Interval spanning several iterations. Kanban and Extreme Programming operate mainly at the single-team level, and Scrum defines no PI, so the other expansions are invented.  Takeaway: SAFe scales teams; PI stands for Planning Interval.
choices: Kanban, and PI stands for Pull Increment, the queue limit for a single team
Extreme Programming, and PI stands for Practice Iteration for engineering work
Scrum, and PI stands for Product Increment produced in one Daily Scrum
SAFe, and PI stands for Planning Interval, the shared cadence used to align many teams

questions.question: A stakeholder asks how acceptance criteria differ from the Definition of Done. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria are the specific testable conditions for a single item, while the Definition of Done is a broader standard every item must meet, so the two operate at different levels. They are not identical, and neither one is a budget or a schedule control.  Takeaway: Acceptance criteria are per-item; the Definition of Done is a broad standard for all items.
choices: They are identical, so a team only needs to maintain one of the two
Acceptance criteria apply to the whole release, while the Definition of Done applies to one item
Acceptance criteria set the budget, while the Definition of Done sets the schedule
Acceptance criteria are specific to one item, while the Definition of Done is a broad standard for all items

questions.question: A hydroelectric dam is expected to take 12 years to design and build. A new team member argues it cannot truly be a project, because 12 years is far too long for anything to be called "temporary." What is the best response?
questions.explanation: Temporary means the endeavor has a defined start and finish, not that it is brief, so even a 12-year build with a definite end is a project. A long duration does not turn a one-time build into operations, and a single dam is not a set of related components forming a program.  Takeaway: Temporary means the effort has a definite end, not that it is short.
choices: The team member is right; any effort lasting more than a few years is too long to count as a project.
It is actually a program, because a multi-year build must be run as a set of related components.
"Temporary" means the endeavor has a definite beginning and end, not that it is short, so the dam build is still a project.
It is operations, because a 12-year effort is so long that it clearly becomes part of the organization's routine, ongoing day-to-day work.

questions.question: A project management office (PMO) requires all projects to adopt specific templates, tools, and governance frameworks and then checks projects for compliance. Which type of PMO is this?
questions.explanation: A controlling PMO requires projects to comply with defined frameworks, templates, and governance and checks for that compliance, giving it a moderate degree of control. A supportive PMO offers guidance and templates with low control, a directive PMO goes further and manages the projects directly with high control, and selecting which projects to fund is a portfolio decision rather than a PMO type.  Takeaway: Supportive PMO = low control, controlling PMO = requires compliance, directive PMO = runs the projects.
choices: Supportive PMO, which provides templates only on request and exercises low control
Directive PMO, which takes over and manages the projects directly
Controlling PMO, which requires compliance with defined frameworks and exercises moderate control
Program office, which exists only to select which projects the organization will fund

questions.question: Which set of artifacts best represents how project controls are documented on a predictive, plan-based project?
questions.explanation: Predictive control relies on approved baselines for scope, schedule, and cost, supported by registers such as the risk register and by status and performance reports that compare actuals against those baselines. Backlogs and burndowns, Kanban boards and cumulative flow diagrams, and story maps and velocity charts are all artifacts of adaptive delivery rather than predictive, plan-based control.  Takeaway: Predictive control artifacts center on baselines, registers, and performance reports; backlogs and burndowns are adaptive.
choices: Product backlog, sprint backlog, and a sprint burndown chart
Kanban board, cumulative flow diagram, and cycle-time chart
Scope, schedule, and cost baselines, a risk register, and status or performance reports
Story map, velocity chart, and iteration retrospective action items

questions.question: Spending on training, process documentation, and design reviews intended to keep defects from occurring falls into which category of the cost of quality?
questions.explanation: Prevention costs are money spent to keep defects from happening in the first place, such as training, documenting processes, and design reviews, and they are a cost of conformance. Appraisal costs (inspection and testing) are also conformance costs but are spent to detect defects rather than only after delivery. Internal and external failure costs are costs of nonconformance, covering rework before delivery and warranty or recall costs after delivery.  Takeaway: Prevention and appraisal are costs of conformance; internal and external failure are costs of nonconformance.
choices: Prevention costs, a cost of conformance
Internal failure costs, a cost of nonconformance
Appraisal costs, incurred only after delivery to the customer
External failure costs, such as warranty claims and recalls

questions.question: Two subject-matter experts hold sharply different, emotionally charged views on how a business rule should handle edge cases, and the analyst must reconcile them before design proceeds. Which communication method fits best?
questions.explanation: Interactive communication such as a working session or conversation supports the real-time give and take needed to reconcile a sensitive, nuanced disagreement. Push and pull methods send or store information but cannot support the back-and-forth, and a memo dictates a rule rather than resolving the conflict behind it.  Takeaway: Use interactive communication for sensitive, nuanced, or conflict situations that need real-time give and take.
choices: Push communication, such as a broadcast email that summarizes both positions to the whole team.
Interactive communication, such as a facilitated working session or a direct conversation.
Pull communication, such as posting both drafts to a shared site for the experts to read later.
Written communication, such as a formal memo that simply states the final rule for the record.

questions.question: A Scrum team wants a simple chart that shows how much work remains in the current sprint as the days pass. Which chart is designed for that view?
questions.explanation: A burndown chart plots remaining work falling toward zero over time, which is exactly the current-sprint view requested. A burnup shows completed work rising toward a scope line, a cumulative flow diagram shows items across states, and a probability-impact matrix rates risks.  Takeaway: A burndown shows remaining work falling over time.
choices: A burndown chart
A burnup chart
A cumulative flow diagram
A probability-impact matrix

questions.question: In a use case for 'Submit Insurance Claim,' the analyst records that the policy must be active before the claim can begin. Which use-case element is this?
questions.explanation: A state that must already be true before a use case can begin, such as an active policy, is a precondition. The main success flow is the normal path once the use case has started, and an exception flow handles deviations rather than entry conditions.  Takeaway: A condition that must be true before a use case begins is a precondition.
choices: The main success flow, the normal step-by-step path to the goal
An exception flow, which handles what happens when the normal path cannot continue
A precondition, a state that must be true before the use case starts
The primary actor, the party that initiates the interaction with the system

questions.question: Without consulting anyone or using any change process, a landscaper adds a decorative fountain and imported stone edging the client never requested, saying "it makes the garden pop." What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: Gold-plating occurs when the team adds features or polish the customer did not ask for, which describes the unrequested fountain and stone edging. Scope creep comes from uncontrolled changes to requested scope, and this addition originates with the team rather than from an approved change or normal elaboration.  Takeaway: When the team adds unrequested extras, that is gold-plating.
choices: Scope creep that was driven by the client's own repeated requests.
Gold-plating, because the team added extras the customer never requested.
An approved change that was properly recorded against the scope baseline.
Progressive elaboration of the project's requirements over time.

questions.question: Which three components together make up the scope baseline?
questions.explanation: The scope baseline is the approved combination of the project scope statement, the WBS, and the WBS dictionary. The other groups mix in schedule/cost baselines, initiating documents, or adaptive artifacts, none of which forms the scope baseline.  Takeaway: Scope baseline = scope statement + WBS + WBS dictionary.
choices: The project scope statement, the WBS, and the WBS dictionary.
The schedule baseline, the cost baseline, and the quality baseline.
The charter, the business case, and the risk register.
The product backlog, the sprint backlog, and the increment.

questions.question: Before planning the next sprint, a team subtracts holidays and planned leave to estimate the effort its members can supply. Which term names what they have just calculated?
questions.explanation: Capacity is the effort a team can supply for the upcoming sprint after accounting for leave, holidays, and other commitments. Velocity is instead a historical measure of completed work, and throughput and lead time are flow metrics, so none of those names available upcoming effort.  Takeaway: Capacity is available effort ahead; velocity is past completed work.
choices: Velocity, the historical work completed in prior sprints
Throughput, the number of items finished per unit of time
Capacity, the effort available for the upcoming sprint
Lead time, the elapsed time from request to delivery

questions.question: A team member is asked to sign a form certifying that all testing is complete, but they know two required test suites were skipped to save time. What does the Code of Ethics direct them to do?
questions.explanation: Honesty requires providing accurate information and not making false statements, so the credited action is to refuse to certify completion and report the true status. Signing a false certification, or signing while staying silent about the gap, both conflict with the duty to be truthful and to take responsibility.  Takeaway: Do not certify something as done that you know is not; report the true status.
choices: Sign the form now and quietly run the skipped suites later if there is spare time.
Sign it, because a manager asked for it and following instructions comes first.
Decline to certify completion and report the true testing status accurately.
Sign it but add no comment, so the skipped suites are technically not denied.

questions.question: A project manager is selecting communication methods. Select the TWO situations where push communication is the most appropriate choice.
questions.explanation: Push communication broadcasts information one way to recipients, which fits notifying a large workforce of a fixed maintenance window and distributing a routine status report. Working through a disagreement and clarifying an ambiguous requirement need interactive back and forth, while a rarely used reference manual looked up on demand is pull communication.  Takeaway: Push broadcasts one-way to recipients; interactive is for give and take, pull is for on-demand lookup.
choices: Working through a tense disagreement between two stakeholders to reach a joint decision.
Notifying a large, dispersed workforce of a fixed maintenance window with no discussion needed.
Clarifying an ambiguous requirement in real time with the person who first raised it.
Distributing a routine weekly status report to a standing distribution list of recipients.
Publishing a rarely used reference manual for staff to look up whenever they need it.

questions.question: A streaming service rolls out a new platform as a sequence of complete, usable feature releases, and viewers can begin using each release the moment it ships. Which delivery approach does this describe?
questions.explanation: Incremental delivery builds the product in usable pieces, each adding functionality customers can start using, which matches shipping successive usable releases. Iterative delivery instead refines the same work over repeated cycles, and handing everything over in one final release is characteristic of predictive or waterfall work.  Takeaway: Incremental delivery adds usable pieces of the product over time.
choices: Iterative, because the same feature is polished repeatedly until it is right.
Incremental, because each release adds a usable piece of the finished product.
Predictive, because the whole platform is handed over in one single final release.
Waterfall, because the project phases are carried out strictly one after another.

questions.question: An analyst is sorting current work into operations versus projects. Choose TWO items that are best classified as operations. (Choose TWO.)
questions.explanation: Operations are the ongoing, repetitive activities that keep the business running, which describes the recurring monthly billing cycle and the continuously staffed security desk. Building a warehouse, a one-time payroll cutover, and a single logo design are each temporary efforts producing a unique result, so they are projects rather than operations.  Takeaway: Repetitive, sustaining work is operations; temporary unique efforts are projects.
choices: Running the monthly customer-billing cycle on the same schedule each month.
Constructing a new regional distribution warehouse to open next year.
Migrating the company to a new payroll system in a one-time cutover.
Staffing the 24-hour security monitoring desk day in and day out.
Designing a brand-new corporate logo for a single rebranding launch.

questions.question: A team member finds a calculation error in a status report that was already sent to the client. Applying the PMI Code's value of honesty, what should they do?
questions.explanation: Honesty in the PMI Code means providing accurate information in a timely manner and correcting errors promptly, so the credited action is to disclose and supply the corrected figures. Concealing, delaying, or asking the client to ignore the error all violate honesty.  Takeaway: Honesty = disclose and correct errors promptly, even when it is uncomfortable.
choices: Promptly inform the client of the error and provide the corrected figures.
Wait to see whether anyone notices before mentioning it.
Quietly correct it in the next report without telling anyone.
Ask the client to overlook it so the schedule is not affected.

questions.question: What is the Scrum Master primarily accountable for on a Scrum Team?
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master establishes Scrum, coaches the team, and helps cause impediments to be removed - a servant/true-leader role. Ordering the backlog is the Product Owner's accountability, building the product is the Developers' work, and there is no formal customer-acceptance gate owned by the Scrum Master.  Takeaway: Scrum Master = establishes Scrum, coaches, and clears impediments (servant leader).
choices: Establishing Scrum, coaching the team, and helping remove impediments as a servant leader.
Ordering the product backlog and deciding item priority.
Personally writing all of the code and tests.
Formally accepting the increment on the customer's behalf.

questions.question: A vendor delivering under a firm fixed-price contract in a regulated pharmaceutical setting insists the contract type by itself makes a fully predictive approach mandatory. What is the best response?
questions.explanation: Contract type and regulatory setting influence the controls, documentation, and governance a project needs, but they do not by themselves dictate the development approach; suitability turns on how stable and well understood the requirements are and how much change is expected. Adaptive or hybrid delivery can operate within fixed-price or regulated contexts with appropriate governance. Claims that fixed-price always requires predictive, or that regulation always forbids or always requires adaptive, each overstate a single factor.  Takeaway: Fixed-price and regulated settings do not auto-require predictive; suitability depends on requirement stability and expected change.
choices: Disagree; the suitable approach depends on requirement stability and expected change, not the contract type alone
Agree; a firm fixed-price contract removes all scope uncertainty, so predictive is required
Agree; regulated pharmaceutical work legally prohibits any iterative or adaptive delivery
Disagree, but only because regulated work must always be adaptive to satisfy inspectors

questions.question: A government agency is migrating its payroll system to comply with a newly passed tax law. The requirements are fixed by statute, the technical solution is well understood, and virtually no change is expected once the plan is set. Which development approach best fits?
questions.explanation: A predictive approach fits work whose scope is defined up front and stable, whose solution is well understood, and where change is unlikely, so it can be planned in detail and executed against baselines. Adaptive approaches earn their value under uncertainty and volatility, which is the opposite of the stability described. Wanting frequent sprints is a signal for an adaptive cadence, not a justification for choosing predictive.  Takeaway: Predictive fits stable, well-understood scope with low expected change; uncertainty and frequent increments point to adaptive.
choices: Adaptive, because public-sector projects must deliver a working increment every iteration
Adaptive, because legally fixed requirements are best handled through continuous re-planning
Predictive, because the requirements are stable, the solution is well understood, and change is unlikely
Predictive, because the agency wants to demonstrate progress in short, frequent sprints

questions.question: During execution, an event that no one had identified or planned for suddenly halts a critical supplier feed, and no response for it exists in the risk register. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.explanation: A workaround is an unplanned response used when a risk that was not identified, or has no planned response, actually occurs. Applying a pre-approved response is impossible because none exists, and logging it as an assumption or a milestone does not address the disruption.  Takeaway: Use a workaround for an unplanned event; follow the planned response when one exists.
choices: Develop a workaround to respond to the unplanned event
Apply the pre-approved response already written for this event
Record it as an assumption and continue exactly as planned
Treat it as a milestone and simply update the schedule marker

questions.question: A developer has just finished a task and, with the product backlog already ordered, is deciding what to do next and how to know the next item succeeds. Which two statements reflect good adaptive practice? (Choose TWO.)
questions.explanation: Good practice is to pull the highest-priority ready item and to confirm its acceptance criteria up front so everyone agrees what success means before work begins. Choosing the easiest or lowest-priority item ignores the ordered backlog, and defining success only after delivery leaves the target unclear during the work.  Takeaway: Pull the highest-priority ready item and agree its acceptance criteria first.
choices: Pull whichever item is easiest, ignoring the backlog order
Pull the highest-priority item that is ready to be worked on
Set success only after the item is delivered, based on how it turned out
Confirm the item's acceptance criteria so success is clear before starting
Pull the lowest-priority item first to clear the bottom of the backlog

questions.question: A project must make 600 retail associates aware of a store-hours change effective next week. No discussion is required, only broad awareness by the date. Which method is most efficient?
questions.explanation: Push communication such as a bulk announcement or posted notice broadcasts one-way awareness efficiently to a large group by a deadline. Individual conversations do not scale to 600 people for a simple notice, pull methods risk associates never looking it up, and a negotiation workshop is for building agreement, not announcing a set change.  Takeaway: Use push communication to broadcast awareness to a large audience by a deadline.
choices: Interactive one-on-one conversations held individually with each of the associates in turn.
Pull communication that depends on each associate searching an intranet page on their own.
Push communication, such as a bulk announcement or a posted notice sent to all associates.
A facilitated negotiation workshop convened for all 600 associates gathered together.

questions.question: What is the difference between the cost baseline and the cost management plan?
questions.explanation: A baseline is an approved reference to measure against (the time-phased budget), while a subsidiary management plan describes HOW an area will be planned and controlled. Option C reverses the two, and both belong to the project management plan, not a product plan.  Takeaway: Baseline = the approved yardstick; management plan = how you'll manage that area.
choices: The cost baseline is the approved, time-phased budget to measure performance against; the cost management plan describes how costs will be planned, estimated, and controlled.
They are two names for the same document.
The cost baseline explains the estimating method, while the cost management plan is the approved budget figure.
Both are components of the product management plan, not the project management plan.

questions.question: A county library replaces its walk-in-only book reservation system with an online catalog so residents can reserve titles from home instead of coming to a branch. Viewing the project as a vehicle for change, what has it fundamentally done?
questions.explanation: A project acts as a vehicle for change by moving an organization from its current state to a desired future state through the outputs it delivers, which here is the online catalog enabling remote reservations. It does not leave the current process untouched, guarantee strategic success, or eliminate the ongoing operations that sustain the new capability.  Takeaway: Projects move an organization from a current state to a desired future state.
choices: It left the county's current reservation process untouched while merely adding a few weekly status reports.
It gave the county a firm, certain guarantee that its wider digital strategy would definitely succeed.
It moved the county from its current walk-in state to a desired future state through the output it delivered.
It permanently removed any need for the county to run ongoing reservation operations after go-live.

questions.question: A manager new to agile tells the team that adopting agile means they can now skip all planning and just start coding whatever they like. How should the team lead best reframe the agile mindset?
questions.explanation: The agile mindset does not abandon planning; it plans continuously and in smaller increments so plans adapt as the team learns. Claiming agile removes planning entirely or fixes one immovable plan up front both misrepresent how adaptive teams work.  Takeaway: Agile spreads planning across the work rather than removing it.
choices: Agile still plans continuously and just spreads planning across the work instead of doing it all up front
Agile eliminates planning completely so that the team can begin coding immediately without any structure
Agile requires one exhaustive plan at the start that the team must never revisit or change afterward
Agile removes the need for any priorities so developers can choose tasks in any order they wish

questions.question: A children's hospital is coordinating a new electronic health record, a telehealth platform, and a linked patient-portal app under a single leader, because integrating them delivers safer, better-connected pediatric care that none of them could achieve on its own. What is this grouping best called?
questions.explanation: A program is a group of related components managed in a coordinated way to gain benefits not available from managing them individually, which fits these interdependent care initiatives. A portfolio groups components chosen to advance strategy and they need not be related, and a single project would not contain several distinct initiatives.  Takeaway: Related components managed together for a shared benefit form a program.
choices: A portfolio, because several funded initiatives are being managed together across the whole hospital.
A single project, because the combined work produces one unified patient-care result for the hospital.
An operation, because the coordinated effort supports the hospital's ongoing day-to-day clinical services.
A program, because related components are managed together to gain benefits not available separately.

questions.question: A team using MoSCoW labels several items 'Won't have (this time).' What does that label mean?
questions.explanation: The Won't-have-this-time category means the team has agreed the items are out of scope for the current timebox, not that they are gone forever, so they can be revisited later. They are not the highest priority, and they are deliberately excluded now rather than promised if time allows.  Takeaway: MoSCoW's Won't-have-this-time means out of scope for now, not permanently deleted.
choices: The items are the highest priority and must ship in the current release
The items are agreed as out of scope for now but may be reconsidered later
The items are permanently removed from the product and can never return
The items are optional extras that will definitely ship if any time remains

questions.question: An IT operations team abandons fixed-length sprints and instead caps how many tickets can be active at once, pulling the next ticket only as capacity opens. Which approach does this describe?
questions.explanation: Kanban is a flow-based method built on limiting work in progress and pulling new work as capacity allows, without fixed iterations. Scrum relies on fixed sprints, Extreme Programming centers on engineering practices, and SAFe scales teams, so none of those matches a WIP-limited pull system.  Takeaway: Kanban is flow-based: WIP limits and pull, no fixed iterations.
choices: Scrum, because work is packaged into fixed-length sprints
Extreme Programming, because it centers on coding practices
SAFe, because it aligns many teams over a planning interval
Kanban, because it is flow-based with WIP limits and pull

questions.question: Between sprints, a product owner reorders several backlog items after learning of a shift in customer demand. A stakeholder asks which change control board signed off on this. What is the best response?
questions.explanation: Reprioritizing and reordering the product backlog is expected, routine work owned by the product owner and does not require formal change control. Formal change requests and control boards are typical of predictive, plan-based governance; adaptive and hybrid projects can still apply formal governance where warranted, but ordinary backlog reprioritization does not go through a change control board.  Takeaway: Backlog reordering is routine PO work, not formal change control.
choices: Reordering the backlog is routine product owner work, not formal change control
A change control board must approve every backlog reordering in advance
Reordering first requires a formal change request and an impact analysis
Only the Scrum Master may reorder the backlog, and only after sign-off

questions.question: A new team member believes the five process groups are the same as project phases run in strict, one-time sequence. What is the correct understanding?
questions.explanation: Process groups (Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring & Controlling, Closing) are categories of activity that overlap and recur across the project and within phases; they are not sequential phases.
